vocabulary.meaning_en: a heavy hand tool with a metal head, used to hit nails
vocabulary.example: He used a hammer to put the picture hook in the wall.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool for turning screws
vocabulary.note_ar: screw = برغي، driver = الذي يدفع/يقود، فالكلمة تعني «الذي يلفّ البرغي»
vocabulary.example: I need a small screwdriver to open the battery cover.
vocabulary.note_en: screw + driver (something that pushes or turns), so the word means "the tool that turns a screw".

vocabulary.meaning_en: a metal tool for holding and turning nuts and bolts
vocabulary.note_ar: wrench أمريكي، spanner بريطاني. حرف w صامت في wrench: تُنطق /rentʃ/
vocabulary.example: Pass me the wrench so I can tighten this bolt.
vocabulary.note_en: "Wrench" is American, "spanner" is British. The "w" in "wrench" is silent: /rentʃ/

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with two handles for holding, bending or cutting wire
vocabulary.note_ar: تأتي دائماً بصيغة الجمع: a pair of pliers
vocabulary.example: Use the pliers to bend the wire.
vocabulary.note_en: Always plural: a pair of pliers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool for making holes
vocabulary.note_ar: drill كفعل = يثقب، وأيضاً تدريب (fire drill = تدريب على الحريق)
vocabulary.example: We need a drill to make holes for the shelf.
vocabulary.note_en: As a verb, "drill" means to make a hole. It also means a practice exercise (fire drill = practice for a fire).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with a sharp toothed blade for cutting wood or metal
vocabulary.note_ar: انتبه: saw أيضاً هي الماضي من see
vocabulary.example: He cut the board in half with a saw.
vocabulary.note_en: Careful: "saw" is also the past tense of "see".

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thin smooth pointed piece of metal that you hit with a hammer
vocabulary.example: Hit the nail gently so the wood doesn't crack.
vocabulary.note_en: "Nail" also means the hard part at the end of your finger.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a pointed metal pin with a spiral thread that you turn into a surface
vocabulary.example: One screw is missing from the door handle.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thick metal pin with a flat end, fixed with a nut
vocabulary.example: The two metal parts are joined with a bolt and a nut.
vocabulary.note_en: It is fixed with a nut.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small piece of metal with a hole that screws onto a bolt
vocabulary.example: Tighten the nut with a wrench.
vocabulary.note_en: "Nut" also means a type of dry fruit, like an almond.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a strong hat that protects your head
vocabulary.note_ar: hard hat أشيع في أمريكا لمواقع البناء، helmet تُستخدم في كل مكان (البناء والدراجات)
vocabulary.example: Everyone on the building site must wear a hard hat.
vocabulary.note_en: "Hard hat" is more common in America for building sites; "helmet" is used everywhere (building, cycling).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a movable set of steps you use to reach high places
vocabulary.example: Hold the ladder while I change the light bulb.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a box for keeping tools in
vocabulary.example: All my tools are in the red toolbox.
vocabulary.note_en: tool + box

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long strip marked with units, used for measuring
vocabulary.example: Use a tape measure to check the width of the window.

vocabulary.meaning_en: coverings that protect your hands
vocabulary.example: Wear gloves when you carry the glass.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a bright jacket without sleeves that helps people see you
vocabulary.note_ar: في بريطانيا يقولون hi-vis اختصار high visibility = رؤية عالية
vocabulary.example: Road workers wear safety vests so drivers can see them.
vocabulary.note_en: In Britain people say "hi-vis", short for "high visibility" (easy to see).

vocabulary.meaning_en: the tools and machines needed for a job
vocabulary.note_ar: اسم غير معدود: لا نقول an equipment ولا equipments
vocabulary.example: The office bought new equipment this year.
vocabulary.note_en: Uncountable noun: don't say "an equipment" or "equipments".

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small tool that joins papers with thin metal pins
vocabulary.example: Can I borrow your stapler for these pages?
vocabulary.note_en: A staple is the small metal pin a stapler puts in paper.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a cover for keeping papers together
vocabulary.example: Put the contracts in the blue folder.
vocabulary.note_en: From "fold" = to bend paper over.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a white board you write on with special pens
vocabulary.example: The manager drew the plan on the whiteboard.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thick pen for writing on boards
vocabulary.example: This marker is dry. Do you have another one?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a machine that makes copies of documents
vocabulary.example: The photocopier is out of paper again.
vocabulary.note_en: In American offices it is often shortened to "copier".

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small machine for doing sums
vocabulary.example: She checked the total with a calculator.
vocabulary.note_en: From "calculate" = to work out numbers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: headphones with a small microphone
vocabulary.example: He wears a headset to answer customer calls.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the programs that a computer uses
vocabulary.note_ar: اسم غير معدود: لا نقول a software، بل a piece of software أو a program
vocabulary.example: The company installed new accounting software.
vocabulary.note_en: Uncountable noun: don't say "a software"; say "a piece of software" or "a program".

vocabulary.meaning_en: the set of keys you type on
vocabulary.example: Don't eat over your keyboard.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small device you move to control a computer
vocabulary.example: My mouse stopped working, so I used the touchpad.
vocabulary.note_en: Plural: mice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the part of a computer that shows pictures and text
vocabulary.example: Clean the screen with a soft dry cloth.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a device that puts power into a battery
vocabulary.example: I forgot my phone charger at home.
vocabulary.note_en: From "charge" = to fill a battery with power.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a machine or tool made for a special job, often electronic
vocabulary.note_ar: device اسم، أما devise فعل معناه يبتكر
vocabulary.example: Please switch off all devices during the exam.
vocabulary.note_en: "Device" is a noun; "devise" is a verb meaning to invent or plan.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to stay away from something harmful
vocabulary.note_ar: يأتي بعده الفعل بـ ing: avoid touching
vocabulary.example: Avoid touching the machine while it is hot.
vocabulary.note_en: Followed by a verb with -ing: avoid touching.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to let liquid fall out by accident
vocabulary.example: I spilled coffee on my desk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make something newer with the latest changes
vocabulary.example: Update your phone to fix the security problem.
vocabulary.note_en: As a noun, "update" means new information or a new version.

vocabulary.meaning_en: official written advice on how to do something
vocabulary.example: Read the safety guidelines before you start.

vocabulary.meaning_en: doing a job well without wasting time or money
vocabulary.example: The new printer is fast and efficient.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make something firmer or more fixed
vocabulary.example: Tighten the screws so the shelf doesn't move.
vocabulary.note_en: tight + en; the opposite is "loosen".

vocabulary.meaning_en: not firmly fixed
vocabulary.example: One of the wheels is loose.
vocabulary.note_en: Don't confuse it with "lose" (to not have something any more).

fine_lines.title: nail vs screw vs bolt
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الثلاثة تُستخدم لتثبيت الأشياء، لكن طريقة العمل مختلفة. nail مسمار أملس ندقّه بالمطرقة hammer. screw برغي له سنّ حلزوني يحفر طريقه داخل الخشب أو الجدار، ونلفّه بالمفك screwdriver. bolt مسمار سداسي سميك طرفه غير مدبّب، يمرّ من ثقب جاهز في القطعتين ويُقفل بصامولة nut ونشدّه بمفتاح الربط wrench.

examples.sentence: He hammered a nail into the wall.
Turn the screw clockwise to tighten it.
The wheel is held on by four bolts.

fine_lines.explanation_en: All three hold things together, but they work differently. A nail is smooth and you hit it with a hammer. A screw has a spiral line around it that cuts its way into wood or a wall, and you turn it with a screwdriver. A bolt is thick with a flat end; it goes through a ready hole in two pieces, is locked with a nut, and you tighten it with a wrench.

fine_lines.title: must vs have to vs should
fine_lines.explanation_ar: must إلزام قاطع 100% خاصة في قواعد السلامة، ومخالفته قد تسبب خطراً حقيقياً. have to إلزام يأتي من الخارج: لائحة الشركة أو القانون أو روتين الوظيفة، وليس مسألة حياة أو موت. should نصيحة مهنية: الأفضل أن تفعل كذا، ولا يوجد عقاب إذا لم تفعل.

examples.sentence: You must wear a helmet on the building site.
Staff have to send their reports by Thursday.
You should keep your tools in order.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Must" is a 100% strong rule, especially for safety; breaking it can be really dangerous. "Have to" is an obligation from outside: company rules, the law or the job routine, not a matter of life and death. "Should" is professional advice: it is better to do it, but there is no punishment if you don't.

fine_lines.title: ladder vs stairs
fine_lines.explanation_ar: ladder سلّم خفيف متنقّل نحمله بأيدينا من مكان لآخر لنصل إلى الأماكن العالية. stairs درج ثابت مبني داخل البيت أو العمارة.

examples.sentence: He climbed the ladder to fix the roof.
Take the stairs to the second floor.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A ladder is light and you carry it from place to place to reach high places. Stairs are fixed steps built inside a house or building.

fine_lines.title: helmet vs hard hat
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان لحماية الرأس. hard hat خوذة العمال في مواقع البناء وهي أشيع في أمريكا. helmet كلمة عامة تُستخدم في كل مكان: البناء وركوب الدراجة والدراجة النارية.

examples.sentence: Visitors must put on a hard hat before entering the site.
Always wear a helmet when you ride a bike.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both protect your head. A hard hat is what workers wear on building sites, and the word is more common in America. "Helmet" is a general word used everywhere: building, cycling and riding a motorbike.

expressions.meaning_ar: عنده مسمار مفكوك في دماغه / تصرفاته غريبة وغير عاقلة
expressions.example: He climbed the ladder without holding it? He must have a screw loose!
expressions.meaning_en: to act in a strange or crazy way

expressions.phrase: use the right tool for the job
expressions.example: Use the right tool for the job and you'll finish faster.
expressions.meaning_en: choose the correct tool for each task

expressions.example: All new workers must follow the safety guidelines.
Keep your desk organized so you can find things quickly.
expressions.meaning_en: to keep something tidy and in order

expressions.phrase: out of paper / out of ink
expressions.example: The printer is out of ink again.
expressions.meaning_en: there is no paper / no ink left

grammar.title: must, have to and should
grammar.explanation_ar: must للإلزام القاطع غالباً في قواعد السلامة. have to للإلزام الذي تفرضه الشركة أو القانون أو روتين العمل. should للنصيحة والتوجيه الإيجابي بلا عقاب. بعد الثلاثة يأتي الفعل في صورته الأساسية بدون to (ما عدا have to نفسها).
examples: You must wear gloves near the saw.
We have to finish the report by Friday.
You should update your computer every month.
grammar.explanation_en: "Must" is for a strong obligation, often in safety rules. "Have to" is for an obligation that comes from the company, the law or the work routine. "Should" is for advice and helpful suggestions, with no punishment. After all three, use the base form of the verb without "to" (except "have to" itself).

grammar.title: mustn't vs don't have to
grammar.explanation_ar: في النفي يتغيّر المعنى تماماً. mustn't = ممنوع منعاً باتاً. don't have to = لست مضطراً، والأمر اختياري حسب رغبتك.
examples: You mustn't spill drinks near the charger. (ممنوع)
You don't have to wear gloves in the office. (غير مضطر)
grammar.explanation_en: In the negative, the meaning changes completely. "Mustn't" = it is strictly forbidden. "Don't have to" = it is not necessary; you can choose.

grammar.title: Uncountable nouns: software, equipment
grammar.explanation_ar: بعض الأسماء غير معدودة فلا نضع قبلها a ولا نجمعها بـ s. نقول software و equipment، وإذا أردنا واحدة نقول a piece of.
grammar.explanation_en: Some nouns are uncountable, so we don't put "a" before them or add -s. We say "software" and "equipment", and for one item we say "a piece of".

questions.question: Which tool do you use to hit a nail?
questions.explanation_ar: المطرقة hammer هي التي ندقّ بها المسامير.
questions.explanation_en: A hammer is the tool we use to hit nails.

questions.question: A bolt is usually fixed with a ___.
questions.explanation_ar: المسمار السداسي bolt يُقفل بصامولة nut.
questions.explanation_en: A bolt is locked with a nut.

questions.question: "You don't have to wear gloves in the office" means:
choices: It is forbidden to wear gloves.
questions.explanation_ar: don't have to = لست مضطراً، الأمر اختياري.
questions.explanation_en: "Don't have to" = it is not necessary; you can choose.

questions.question: Which sentence means "it is forbidden"?
choices: You mustn't spill drinks near the charger.
You don't have to spill drinks.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.explanation_ar: software اسم غير معدود فلا نضع a ولا نجمعه.
questions.explanation_en: "Software" is uncountable, so no "a" and no plural -s.

questions.question: A movable set of steps you carry to reach high places is a:
questions.explanation_ar: ladder سلّم متنقّل، أما stairs فدرج ثابت في المبنى.
questions.explanation_en: A ladder can be moved; stairs are fixed in a building.

questions.question: Your friend's marker is very weak. You give advice: "You ___ get a new one."
questions.explanation_ar: هذه نصيحة بسيطة وليست إلزاماً، فنستخدم should.
questions.explanation_en: This is simple advice, not an obligation, so we use "should".

questions.question: "He has a screw loose" means he:
choices: acts in a strange, crazy way
questions.explanation_ar: have a screw loose = تصرفاته غريبة وغير عاقلة.
questions.explanation_en: "Have a screw loose" = to act in a strange or crazy way.

questions.question: Which word has a silent letter?
Be careful not to ___ your coffee on the keyboard.
questions.explanation_en: Spill = to make a liquid fall out by accident.
